headline_method: Headline: AR256 isolated layer minus the matched L0 removal (4230), plus the largest measured chain increment of the stream (8 cycles: stream L0/L1/L2 = 4967/4967/4975, i.e. write-back meets refresh costs <=8 cycles under stream-aware REFpb), for L1..L35. The per-layer subtraction (upper bound) lands below the isolated composition because the AR256 chain penalties differ from the W12 ones; it is not used.
method: Matched A/B on the W12 REAL_MEM runtime (frozen_v2 real2 vs HBM_STREAM WBW=4, same core, same position oracle, both bit-exact): cycles removed per layer = real2 - stream. Applied to the AR256 REAL_MEM full-token record (main 973abe581: E 98, L0 chained 4,337 / isolated 4,338, L1 4,776, L2 4,653, head 3,006; token 172,484 chained-adjusted = head + E + L0 + 35 x mean(L1,L2)). Assumes the memory stall removed is the same in the AR256 core (same KV service boundary, same fill/drain MEMSTAT counters); the AR256 core's real-minus-ideal penalty is larger (+383 at L0 vs +247), so the removal is not over-credited.
